summary:
TerraHub — Intelligence that protects your harvest.

TerraHub is a hybrid agricultural intelligence platform designed to help small and medium-sized farmers make better-informed decisions about soil, climate, and crop selection, starting with a demonstration scenario in Cianorte, Paraná, in southern Brazil. The solution combines geospatial analysis, environmental and weather data from NASA POWER, agronomic references from Embrapa (Saúde do Solo BR / BioAS), and official guidelines from Brazil’s Agricultural Zoning of Climate Risk program (ZARC/MAPA). It turns complex technical variables into interactive maps, transparent alerts, and practical guidance through an AI assistant that communicates in accessible language.

The project addresses the challenge of making spatial and climate data intelligence more accessible to family farmers and medium-sized producers, who often face technical barriers when interpreting multiple data sources, limited visibility into differences between fields, and high exposure to extreme weather events. This approach is essential to reducing preventable crop losses, improving harvest planning, and strengthening financial and environmental resilience in rural communities.
details:
• What exactly does the project do? TerraHub organizes registration and geographic information about rural properties and their fields, combining historical climate data, soil indicators, and agricultural zoning guidelines. It then provides dashboards with clear indicators, thematic maps, preventive alerts (heat, rainfall, and signs of water stress), guidance on crop suitability, and a conversational AI assistant that explains results in plain language while identifying each data source, time period, and limitation.
    • Farmers create an account and register their property (name, municipality, state, land registry number as a reference, area, and coordinates).
    • The system maps the property and its fields in an interactive map.
    • The platform retrieves historical weather and solar energy data from the NASA POWER API for the selected coordinates and time period.
    • Users manually enter soil laboratory results, clearly distinguishing measured, estimated, and unavailable values.
    • A rules engine generates transparent alerts and compares suitable crops using references from ZARC (MAPA) and regional indicators from Embrapa.
    • An AI assistant, grounded exclusively in the data available in the system, answers farmers’ questions without making up information and points out any data gaps.
    • Translates complex climate, geospatial, and agronomic data into understandable guidance.
    • Provides field-level visibility within each property.
    • Ensures transparency and reliability by clearly distinguishing historical data, weather forecasts, regional data, and local laboratory analyses—and labeling demonstration data as simulated.
    • Reduces exposure to climate risks, crop losses, and debt resulting from poorly informed planting decisions.
  • What do we hope to achieve? Validate the experience and usefulness of the MVP’s core workflow with small and medium-sized farmers and professionals in the Cianorte region of Paraná. In future phases, the platform may be expanded with WhatsApp Business Cloud API integration, short-term weather forecasts from INMET, an economic module, and aggregated regional dashboards for cooperatives, agricultural extension services, and input distributors.
    • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
    • Maps and geospatial processing: Leaflet or MapLibre.
    • Backend: Python with FastAPI.
    • Database: PostgreSQL with the PostGIS spatial extension.
    • Integrations and AI: NASA POWER API and a language model (LLM) API grounded in the system’s data, with an architecture planned for WhatsApp Business Cloud API integration in a later phase.
    • Development support: ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Codex for conceptual structuring, requirements, and initial code generation.
